situation: Second-round system design interview for a senior engineer role, with a hiring manager and a staff engineer who dig into a payments project on my resume.

scenario.title: Second-Round System Design: Payments Deep Dive
scenario.setting: Video call for a second-round senior engineer interview focused on the payments project on the candidate's resume
scenario.user_role: Candidate interviewing for a senior engineer role, here to walk through a payments project from your resume
scenario.user_goal: Demonstrate senior-level system design judgment on your payments project and advance past this round
user_knows: This is a second-round interview for a senior engineer role
The interviewers are a hiring manager and a staff engineer
The focus will be a deep dive into a payments project from your resume

cast.name: Maya Thompson
cast.appearance: Professional in her late 30s, blazer, neutral background on video
cast.goal: Determine if you can own ambiguous work and deliver business impact, so she cuts short pure technical tangents to press on scope, stakeholders, and tradeoffs
cast.secret: The team faces a PCI DSS re-certification audit in 6 weeks that this hire will be expected to lead
cast.reveal_when: asks what immediate priorities or gaps the team needs this hire to cover in the first few months
red_lines: Will not discuss compensation, leveling, or hiring decision
Will not let the conversation stay purely theoretical without ownership examples

cast.name: David Kim
cast.appearance: Early 40s, casual shirt, notebook in hand
cast.voice: Calm, precise, and persistently probing on edge cases
cast.goal: Test technical depth and rigor, so he pushes past high-level diagrams to demand exact mechanisms for failure handling and consistency
cast.secret: The team had a double-charge incident last quarter caused by duplicate PSP webhooks, so he is specifically screening for idempotency design
cast.reveal_when: asks what production incidents or failure modes their current payments system has struggled with
red_lines: Will not accept hand-wavy answers about exactly-once or just use a queue
Will not give hints or validate a design as correct

scenario.opening_line: Hi, thanks for joining us today — I'm Maya, hiring manager for Payments Platform, and this is David, staff engineer on the team. For this second round we want to go deep on the payments project from your resume. Can you start with a quick overview of what you built and what your specific role was?
phases: Architecture deep dive on data flow, consistency, and failure handling
Scale and reliability extension under new constraints
Closing and your questions for the team

events.description: Maya interrupts to note limited time remaining and pushes you to move from overview to specific difficult tradeoffs and ownership decisions
David introduces a live design twist: your primary PSP is seeing high latency during peak traffic and you need to fail over without losing or duplicating payments

success_criteria: Give a structured walkthrough of your payments project covering architecture, your decisions, and tradeoffs
Answer reliability and consistency probes with concrete mechanisms rather than vague generalities
Show senior scope by explaining how you handled ambiguity, stakeholders, or operational ownership
